Breaking: The astonishing, untold story of Marie-Anne “Baby” de Goldschmidt-Rothschild, who smuggled a Van Gogh painting and the artist's letters out of Nazi Europe

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theartnewspaper

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that among the early Van Gogh collectors was a young woman who had just turned 22.
  • Her amazing story is told in a meticulously researched latest book: A Collector’s Odyssey: How Marie-Anne de Goldschmidt-Rothschild saved her Paintings from Nazi Looting, written by Christel Force, Anna-Carolin Augustin and Katharina Weiler and published in Berlin by De Gruyter (it is freely downloadable).
  • Musée d’Orsay, Paris (Donation sous réserve d'usufruit Mme R.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that among the early Van Gogh collectors was a young woman who had just turned 22. Born in 1892 to a very wealthy German family, Marie-Anne (nicknamed “Baby”) de Goldschmidt-Rothschild certainly had the money, but also avant-garde taste. She bought one of the artist’s finest portraits.

Her amazing story is told in a meticulously researched latest book: A Collector’s Odyssey: How Marie-Anne de Goldschmidt-Rothschild saved her Paintings from Nazi Looting, written by Christel Force, Anna-Carolin Augustin and Katharina Weiler and published in Berlin by De Gruyter (it is freely downloadable).

Van Gogh’s The Arlésienne (November 1888).

Musée d’Orsay, Paris (Donation sous réserve d'usufruit Mme R. de Goldschmidt-Rothschild, 1952 © photo : RMN-Grand Palais (Musée d’Orsay) / Stéphane Maréchalle).

It may come as a surprise that the very first painting bought by Marie-Anne (whose maiden name was Friedländer-Fuld) was a Van Gogh - and an vital one. Encouraged by progressive mentors, in June 1914 she purchased The Arlésienne (November 1888), a portrait of the artist’s friend Marie Ginoux, co-owner of the Café de la Gare in Arles. The picture cost the equivalent of £6250, a very large sum for a Van Gogh at the time.

Marie-Anne later recounted how she hung the portrait, on antique-gold wallpaper, in her suite in the family’s palatial residence in Berlin’s Pariser Platz, almost next to the Brandenburg Gate: “My first and only painting, at the centre [of her main room], dominating everything and everyone, was L’Arlésienne by Van Gogh”. Her father, who had much more traditional tastes, abhorred the artist, telling her to hide “the jaundiced old lady” behind a curtain.

Marie-Anne de Goldschmidt-Rothschild, with her Louis XV sofa and Van Gogh’s The Arlésienne in her Berlin mansion (1929).

Photograph by Ernst Schneider, De Querschnitt journal (Berlin), September 1929.

It has been revealed that this was only the beginning. Marie-Anne went on to collect other Impressionist artists and their followers: Paul Gauguin, Claude Monet, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Edouard Manet, Paul Cezanne and Pablo Picasso.

Industry observers note that by the time Marie-Anne was 31, she had married three times: to the English aristocrat John Mitford, the former German foreign minister Richard von Kühlmann and the aristocratic banker Rudolf von Goldschmidt-Rothschild (he used “von”, while she preferred “de”). After a few years, she and Rudolf lived independently and eventually divorced in 1938.

Sources indicate that with the rise of the Nazis, Marie-Anne, who was of Jewish heritage, smuggled the Van Gogh portrait twice. The first time was in 1934, a year after Hitler came to power, when she secretly sent the painting from Berlin to her residence in Paris. This required subterfuge: she commissioned an artist friend, Eugen Spiro, to paint identical copies of her most notable paintings. The copy of The Arlésienne was then surreptitiously placed in the frame in her Berlin mansion, with no one apparently noticing the switch.

The Van Gogh and the other canvasses were taken off their stretchers and rolled up. Marie-Anne instructed Marie-Anne instructed her (female) servants to each carry a single roll to Paris, without telling them what was inside. Had the pictures been declared at the border, Nazi officials would have prevented them from being exported or would have charged her an exorbitant tax. The Arlésienne safely arrived at Marie-Anne's mansion in Paris on the Rue de la Faisanderie.

Industry observers note that six years later, France was threatened by Germany. In mid-May 1940, a month before the Nazi occupation of Paris, Marie-Anne decided to flee to the US, protecting her life and collection. By that time, the only route was via Portugal, which was neutral. In a move which the book’s co-author Force describes as “reckless and admirable in equal measure”, Marie-Anne hatched a strategy for her most important paintings.

Industry observers note that she again took the canvases off their stretchers, rolled them up, disguised the package and strapped it to the roof of her Citroën. Amidst the chaos of millions fleeing Paris, she drove across France to Spain, facing seemingly endless logistical challenges, but eventually reaching Portugal. Although some reports suggest the Van Gogh was transported on the roof with the rest of the paintings, Marie-Anne later told a different story.

It has been revealed that according to her, The Arlésienne had been sent earlier to Amsterdam, on loan for an exhibition. Just one week before the German invasion in May 1940, her contact in the Netherlands somehow managed to get the Van Gogh onto an aircraft bound for Lisbon.

In her hotel room in Portugal, Marie-Anne rolled up all her paintings, although the thick impasto paint of The Arlésienne created problems. She then covered the whole roll with a protective tarpaulin. Eventually she secured a place on a liner crossing the Atlantic, bound for Mexico.

After her ship finally arrived at Veracruz, Marie-Anne travelled on to Mexico City, later taking a plane to Texas and another flight on to New York, accompanied by her paintings. The Arlésienne had been travelling during wartime for nearly five months, arriving in New York in November 1940.

Marie-Anne, thanks to her immense wealth and elite contacts, had managed to escape the terrible fate of the vast majority of continental European Jewry.

Industry observers note that in 1928, Marie-Anne made another prescient purchase: a collection of 22 letters written by Van Gogh in 1887-89 to his artist friend Emile Bernard (plus one to Gauguin). The bulk of Vincent’s surviving letters remained with Theo and his heirs, so the Bernard correspondence represented a very notable acquisition. Many of the letters also included small sketches of the paintings which Van Gogh was working on.

Van Gogh’s letter to Emile Bernard, around 19 June 1888 (extracts).

Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam (Vincent van Gogh Foundation).

When the art lover and writer Harry Kessler visited Marie-Anne in 1929, he noted in his diary that they had dined under The Arlésienne. Kessler then recorded: “After dinner, thirty letters by Van Gogh in an excessively ornate, ugly binding, were passed around with cigarettes and coffee.” (Although Kessler said it was 30 letters, it was actually 23.) Contrasting the opulence with the artist’s simple way of life, Kessler added: “Poor Van Gogh!”.

In a recent development, in 1940, when Marie-Anne fled from Paris in her Citroën, she carried this ornately-bound volume of Van Gogh’s correspondence in a suitcase. She kept the letters during her American wartime exile.

On 26 August 1944, just hours after Paris was liberated, Marie-Anne wrote from California to the Free France delegation in Washington, DC: “My hand is shaking with emotion as I am writing to you today, day of the Liberation of Paris. I turn to you to ask that whoever is concerned be informed that I bequeath my Van Gogh painting L’Arlésienne to the city of Paris. It is at the Louvre, I expect, that it will find its place.”.

It has been revealed that marie-Anne left Upcoming York and returned to Europe in 1947, once again taking her paintings with her. Her family’s palatial residence in Berlin had been almost totally destroyed by Allied bombs, and she wanted to settle in her mansion in Paris. There she would spend the rest of her life, until her death in 1973.

The dining room in Marie-Anne de Goldschmidt-Rothschild’s Paris mansion (1950s).

Photograph by Antoinette Georges Perrier, De Goldschmidt-Rothschild family archive.

Recent findings suggest that marie-Anne had lived with The Arlésienne for nearly 60 years. After her death, the painting went to the Louvre, which displayed it in the Jeu de Paume. It was transferred to the Musée d’Orsay when it opened in 1986.

According to recent reports, we can report that next year The Arlésienne will be presented in an exhibition at the Musée de l’Orangerie in Paris: Dépossédes: Oeuvres spoliées, vies brisées 1933-45 (Dispossessed: Plundered Art, Shattered Lives 1933–45)(October 2027-January 2028). Marie-Anne’s life certainly had its challenges, but it was hardly shattered like most of the other collectors who will be featured in the show.

As for the Van Gogh correspondence, Marie-Anne donated one letter to the Fondation Custodia in Paris, another somehow left her collection and the one addressed to Gauguin was given to a friend. This left 20 letters which she bequeathed to her grandson, Frédéric de Goldschmidt-Rothschild. He sold the group to the Fresh York dealer and collector Eugene Thaw in 2001.

Thaw later recalled how he bought the letters: “A young man [the grandson] showed up in my office with them all under his arm—unframed, unmatted—in a simple folder. And of course I nearly died of pleasant shock at seeing them.” Marie-Anne’s ornate binding had already gone.

It has been revealed that the correspondence was generously donated by Thaw to New York’s Morgan Library & Museum. These key Van Gogh letters, with their 14 sketches, are now reunited online with the rest of the artist’s correspondence, online.

Industry observers note that for conservation reasons, Van Gogh's letters to Bernard are very rarely exhibited, but I once had the privilege of examining the originals in the Morgan’s study room. Seeing the letters, penned by the artist on ordinary writing paper with his little sketches, I thought back to when they had once been housed in Marie-Anne’s ornate album—and their perilous journey during the war.

It has been revealed that martin Bailey is a leading Van Gogh specialist and special correspondent for The Art Newspaper. He has curated exhibitions at the Barbican Art Gallery, Compton Verney/National Gallery of Scotland and Tate Britain.

Martin Bailey’s recent Van Gogh books.

Martin has written a number of bestselling books on Van Gogh’s years in France: The Sunflowers Are Mine: The Story of Van Gogh's Masterpiece (Frances Lincoln 2013, UK and US), Studio of the South: Van Gogh in Provence (Frances Lincoln 2016, UK and US), Starry Night: Van Gogh at the Asylum (White Lion Publishing 2018, UK and US) and Van Gogh’s Finale: Auvers and the Artist’s Rise to Fame (Frances Lincoln 2021, UK and US). The Sunflowers are Mine (2024, UK and US) and Van Gogh’s Finale (2024, UK and US) are also now available in a more compact paperback format.

His other recent books include Living with Vincent van Gogh: The Homes & Landscapes that shaped the Artist (White Lion Publishing 2019, UK and US), which provides an overview of the artist’s life. The Illustrated Provence Letters of Van Gogh has been reissued (Batsford 2021, UK and US). My Friend Van Gogh/Emile Bernard provides the first English translation of Bernard’s writings on Van Gogh (David Zwirner Books 2023, UKand US).

To contact Martin Bailey, please email vangogh@theartnewspaper.com.

Please note that he does not undertake authentications.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Los Angeles-based David Christopher Lee has been a celebrity portrait photographer for 27 years, capturing stars like Lady Gaga, the Kardashians, and Britney Spears.
  • On November 19, Lee attended the premiere of Jennifer Lopez’s The JLo Show at Paramount Studios in Hollywood as a guest of his friend Maximillian Acevedo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A photographer has revealed how he managed to get a credit on Jennifer Lopez’s Instagram account after the star initially reposted his video without any attribution.

Los Angeles-based David Christopher Lee has been a celebrity portrait photographer for 27 years, capturing stars like Lady Gaga, the Kardashians, and Britney Spears.

A post shared by Jennifer Lopez (@jlo).

On November 19, Lee attended the premiere of Jennifer Lopez’s The JLo Show at Paramount Studios in Hollywood as a guest of his friend Maximillian Acevedo. Lee claims he had no intentions of taking any photographs or videos at the event.

In a recent development, however, when Lopez came out on the red carpet, photographers rushed out to take pictures, and Lee couldn’t resist shooting some images of the star herself. Lee moved behind the crowd of photographers to find a different angle of Lopez. He noticed Lopez’s yellow diamond necklace and zoomed in to capture a 13-second video on his iPhone at 5x zoom.

The lighting was particularly good, illuminating Lopez’s jawline and earring, and Lee states he immediately knew he had captured the shot he wanted.

“As all the photographers started calling her name. I bolted for the red carpet and stood in the back looking for the perfect angle and whipped out my iPhone, shooting it on 5x,” Lee tells PetaPixel. “My eyes immediately went to her necklace so I framed it like a jewelry shot and the rest is history. I posted the video immediately on Instagram and it immediately went viral.”.

Lee posted the video to his Instagram account (@davidsguide) at 6:25 PM that day. A few hours later, Lopez’s own Instagram account reposted Lee’s clip to her 239 million followers without crediting or tagging him.

Lee initially did not realize Lopez had reposted his video because the sound was different. But he eventually recognized his camera movement.

“At first I didn’t know it was my video because the sound was different,” Lee notes. “Then I noticed the same movement of my camera and compared them side by side. I was in shock that she had posted it to her 239 million followers, the only video from that night.”.

Lee says he felt both pleased that his video had gone viral and upset that it was shared without credit, leaving viewers unaware he had filmed it.

In a recent development, “Out of the 100 photographers and videographers there, she had posted my video. I was sad and happy at the same time,” Lee explains. “The video was getting millions of views, and nobody knew I shot it. I felt violated because I’m entertainment, the least someone can do is credit you for using your content.”.

Rather than let the video circulate without credit, Lee took matters into his own hands, contacting several members of Lopez’s team before reaching her social media manager, who agreed to credit his work.

According to recent reports, “I reached out to everyone I could find on her team and finally got in touch with her social media manager after five million views,” Lee tells PetaPixel. “I emailed him asking him to credit, and within ten minutes, he replied sorry and gave credit in the video. I felt so accomplished at that point.”.

As of writing, Lopez’s repost, which now includes Lee’s Instagram tag @davidcleephotography, has over 350,000 likes and over 9,600 comments. Lee states that reposting content without attribution can give it a wide audience while leaving the original photographer unrecognized. He believes photographers frequently have their work shared without credit because content spreads so promptly online that people sometimes forget to acknowledge its creator.

It has been revealed that “It happens all the time,” Lee says. “Content moves and travels so fast these days that a lot of times people forget to tag and credit. It is unfortunate, but it’s the world we live in.”.

Industry observers note that lee encourages photographers to learn from his experience and take precautions when sharing their work on social media. He advises them to watermark their images and videos before posting, as they never know how widely the content might be shared.

“The lesson is you never know what can happen with your content and the best thing to do is watermark your pics or videos before posting,” Lee claims.

Recent findings suggest that he adds: “Keep doing what you do and do stop believing in yourself. The possibilities are endless.”.

More of David Christopher’s work can be found on his website and blog David’s Guide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home. Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up! Why are my ears clogged? Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked: Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage. If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection. Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side. Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too. Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure. Best clogged ear remedies 1. Pop and unclog The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes. 2. Swallow, yawn, or chew The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow. 3. Ear drops Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes. Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful. 4. Warmth and gravity To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily. 5. Hit the steam room Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 6. Take allergy medication Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears. Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort. 7. Rinse away the gunk Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing. When to see your doctor Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention. What not to do when you have clogged ears Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries. Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion. Drying solutions: A few drops of rubbing alcohol or a mixture of one part vinegar and one part alcohol can help dry out the ears when you have a swimmer’s ear. However, doing this regularly can lead to irritation. Takeaway Clogged ears are often caused by earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure. You can use over-the-counter or DIY ear drops, irrigation kits, or warm compresses to unblock your ears. Antihistamines or nasal sprays can also help relieve clogs caused by allergies. PSA: Consult a healthcare provider if your blocked ears are painful or at-home remedies don’t work.

"Europe's largest museum development" opens in 1930s Citroën garage in Brussels

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Brussels‘ former Citroën Garage has been transformed into Kanal, a 40,000-square-metre museum for modern art and architecture with an exhibition programme developed with the Parisian art institution Centre Pompidou.
  • The transformation was designed by Atelier Kanal, a consortium made up of architecture studio EM2N, NoAarchitecten and Sergison Bates Architects, with a team of construction workers, who restored the 1930s industrial building and added three latest volumes within its structure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photography by Koen Van Damme unless otherwise stated. Video by Eyes–Screen.

Brussels‘ former Citroën Garage has been transformed into Kanal, a 40,000-square-metre museum for modern art and architecture with an exhibition programme developed with the Parisian art institution Centre Pompidou.

The transformation was designed by Atelier Kanal, a consortium made up of architecture studio EM2N, NoAarchitecten and Sergison Bates Architects, with a team of construction workers, who restored the 1930s industrial building and added three latest volumes within its structure.

Claiming to be “Europe’s largest museum development”, Kanal – sometimes referred to as Kanal-Centre Pompidou – hopes to provide space for people to gather to enjoy visual art, performance, dance, music, film and architecture.

Opening to the public on 28 November, the canal-side building was originally built in 1934 as a garage and showroom for the car company Citroën.

Atelier Kanal aimed to keep the industrial character of the building by implementing a “light touch” approach, restoring most of the building fabric, repairing and upgrading parts where needed, and replacing other parts to improve climatic and acoustic conditions.

The garage’s former showroom, a modernist curved glass building with 20-metre-tall interiors, was converted into a gallery space topped with a publicly accessible rooftop.

“Rather than a spectacular gesture, our proposal offers an attitude of ‘radical optimism’ – open and non-prescriptive, spontaneous and instinctive – much like the spirit of modern progress in which it was created,” remarked Atelier Kanal.

“The interior is a fine example of elegant industrial engineering, while the glass facades clearly express early modernism,” it continued.

“Our ambition has been to trust the building as we found it, embracing its industrial character and many layers of use.”.

Three newly introduced buildings were added inside the existing structure, including a four-storey volume with a basement level that contains art galleries, and another volume housing a 378-seat auditorium and the Kanal offices.

The third volume is the newly introduced home for Brussels’ museum and archive of architecture, Kanal Architecture, which was formerly known as CIVA.

Rising nine stories on the north-east side of the campus, across from the art galleries, the structure includes exhibition spaces, a library, archives, research centre, bookshop and workshop spaces.

Architecture collective Assemble designed an indoor playground on the first floor of the museum, which features playscapes informed by volcanoes, planets, and piles of coal that were once transported on the canal.

Elsewhere in the building are a library, bookshop, rooftop bar, restaurants and an in-house bakery.

Kanal’s year-round programme of exhibitions was developed in collaboration with the Centre Pompidou art museum in Paris.

“Kanal invites citizens, organisations, collectives and communities to appropriate and inhabit large parts of the building, for production, performances, events, informal gatherings or simply to spend time,” said Atelier Kanal.

Industry observers note that “The museum extends beyond curated art, becoming part of the city and its fabric,” it continued. “In this sense, Kanal departs from the traditional museum and instead offers a place for civic gathering, responding to the growing absence of shared public spaces in our cities today.”.

Other museums that have recently opened in historic buildings include the London Museum, located in a transformed Victorian market building, and a bank in Santander that was transformed into the Faro Santander museum.

Photography by Koen Van Damme unless otherwise stated. Video by Eyes–Screen.

That's a 20% improvement in value with zero extra effort. Blueprint longer trips to unlock this.

Do: Book 395 Days Out for Peak Destinations.

Hyatt opens award inventory at the same time as cash inventory — 395 days in advance. For high-demand properties (think Park Hyatt Maldives at Hadahaa or Alila Ventana Big Sur), availability at standard rates disappears quickly. Set a calendar reminder and search early.

Do: Combine With Chase Ultimate Rewards.

Industry observers note that if you hold a Chase Sapphire Preferred or Reserve, your Chase Ultimate Rewards points also transfer to Hyatt at 1:1, instantly. This means you have two separate point pools feeding the same program — Bilt for rent earnings and Chase for everyday spending. Together, you can accumulate Hyatt points significantly faster and take on higher-category properties.

Avoid: Transferring Points Before Confirming Availability.

Bilt-to-Hyatt transfers are instant and irreversible. If you transfer 30,000 points and then can't find the availability you thought you saw, those points are now in Hyatt — and if you don't use them, they expire after 24 months of account inactivity. Always search Hyatt first, confirm dates and property, then transfer.

Avoid: Missing the 5-Transaction Monthly Minimum.

This is the most common Bilt mistake. If you forget to make five purchases on your Bilt card in a given month, you earn zero points on rent — not reduced points, zero. Automate five small recurring charges to the card and never think about it again.

Do: Target Category 4–6 Properties for Best Value.

Sources indicate that category 1–3 properties offer solid value, but the CPP accelerates meaningfully in Categories 4–6 (15,000–25,000 points/night) where cash rates are $200–$400 but points costs haven't kept pace. This is the sweet spot within the sweet spot.

Do: Watch for Hyatt's Points + Cash Awards.

According to recent reports, hyatt offers a Points + Cash option at roughly half the standard award rate, combined with a cash co-pay. If your Hyatt balance is small, this lets you access properties without waiting to accumulate a full award.

This redemption was built for renters — specifically, renters who are already on the path to FI and feel the friction of paying rent every month with nothing to show for it. If you pay at least $1,000/month in rent, this sweet spot is generating meaningful Hyatt points from dollar one. At $2,000/month, you're accumulating 24,000 Hyatt points per year from rent alone — enough for two nights at a Category 5 property or a single aspirational night at a Park Hyatt.

It has been revealed that minimum to make it work: You need at least 5,000 Hyatt points for a Category 1 redemption — easily achievable after 5–6 months of rent payments on a $1,000/month lease. For aspirational Category 6–7 stays, you're targeting 25,000–30,000 points, which takes planning but is absolutely achievable.

This isn't the right fit if you own your home (no rent to earn on), if you're already deep into a competing hotel loyalty program, or if your primary travel goal is international business class flights — in that case, transferable airline currencies deserve more of your attention first. But for hotel stays, especially in the U.S., this is the single most frictionless on-ramp into the Hyatt ecosystem available anywhere.

Sources indicate that this redemption earns a **5/5 for beginner friendliness**, and that rating is accurate — but it helps to understand exactly *why* it's easy, so you don't accidentally make it harder than it needs to be. **What makes it easy:** - Earning is passive. Once your Bilt card is set up and rent is registered, points accrue automatically with no behavior change required (beyond five small monthly transactions). - The transfer is instant — no waiting, no uncertainty, no risk of availability disappearing while points are in transit. - Hyatt's award chart is fixed and transparent. You can see exactly what a property costs before you transfer a single point. - No fuel surcharges means no unpleasant surprises at checkout. **The one area that trips beginners up:** forgetting the five-transaction monthly minimum. This is the single most common Bilt mistake, and it's entirely preventable. Set up five small autopay charges on your Bilt card — a $5 streaming service, a recurring Amazon purchase, anything — and you'll never miss it. **Tip for the first redemption:** Start with a Category 3 or 4 Hyatt Place or Hyatt Regency for a domestic weekend trip. The points requirement is low (8,000–15,000 points), availability is widely open, and the booking process is identical to any other Hyatt stay. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh investigation has uncovered how a brave photographer, who risked his life taking hundreds of pictures of Nazi-occupied France, may have been betrayed by two neighbors.
  • In April 2020, a mysterious album containing hundreds of photos of daily life during the German Nazi occupation of Paris from 1940 to 1942 was discovered in a flea market in Barjac in Gard, France.
  • Paris occupé WW2 pic.twitter.com/SBnUj87HWA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh investigation has uncovered how a brave photographer, who risked his life taking hundreds of pictures of Nazi-occupied France, may have been betrayed by two neighbors.

In April 2020, a mysterious album containing hundreds of photos of daily life during the German Nazi occupation of Paris from 1940 to 1942 was discovered in a flea market in Barjac in Gard, France.

Raoul Minot.1940-42. Paris occupé WW2 pic.twitter.com/SBnUj87HWA.

— Paris Paname (@ParisAMDParis) August 24, 2024.

It has been revealed that le Monde journalist Philippe Broussard began a four-year investigation to identify the photographer, who had taken at least 700 pictures of Paris during the first two years of the Occupation. At the time, unauthorized photography was banned by the Nazis, and taking such pictures could carry the death penalty. In 2024, Broussard identified the photographer as Raoul Minot.

Minot used a “little Kodak Brownie 6/9 camera” and developed the prints in the photographic laboratory of the department store where he worked. He then sold hundreds of his images to the French Resistance, a collection of groups that fought against the Nazi occupation during World War II.

However, Minot’s photographic mission came to an end in November 1942, just two years after it began, when an unidentified informer reported his activities to the Nazis.

Minot was imprisoned and deported to Mauthausen concentration camp in Austria on April 20, 1943, where he was forced to perform labor. He was later transferred to Flossenbürg concentration camp in Bavaria and liberated by U.S. forces on April 23, 1945. He tragically died five days later in a hospital in Cham, Bavaria.

It has been revealed that following his discovery of Minot in 2024, Broussard set out to uncover who had turned in the photographer to the Nazis for a report in Le Monde. A breakthrough came in April 2026, when a reader contacted Le Monde with a document that could help solve the mystery. Jean-Pierre Gross, a local history enthusiast from Courbevoie, France, had discovered a 1944 report accusing two of Minot’s neighbors, Marie Breux and Georges Robinson, of collaborating with the Germans and helping secure the arrests of people suspected of opposing the Occupation.

In a recent development, the report specifically named Minot, stating that the couple were suspected of having “denounced or, at the very least, incriminated” him. It also claimed they had boasted about getting 18 people arrested.

Breux was the building’s concierge, while Robinson, her partner, was a tailor with a history of theft and other criminal convictions. Both were arrested following the Liberation in August 1944, although no record of a conviction against either has been found.

Further investigation revealed that Robinson had briefly worked at the same Printemps department store as Minot, potentially explaining how he knew about the store’s photographic facilities.

Recent findings suggest that broussard later uncovered an anonymous letter sent in December 1942 that accused Minot and his wife of photographing Nazi propaganda posters and bomb damage. The letter prompted a police investigation that led to Minot’s arrest and the seizure of more than 1,000 photographic negatives.

“Sir, could you ask the Minot household, both of whom work at the Printemps — the wife as a cashier, the husband as a warehouse manager — whether their jobs qualify them to take photographs of propaganda posters and air raid damage to our poor country?” the letter reads. “We don’t think it would be very useful to inform you about the troubled times France is going through, thanks to many workers in troubled waters.

According to Le Monde, a handwriting expert subsequently ruled out Robinson as the author of the anonymous letter that triggered the investigation into Minot, but could not exclude Breux. Broussard believes the couple may have worked together to report Minot after discovering that he was photographing Nazi propaganda posters and bomb damage around Courbevoie.

Although there is still no conclusive evidence to establish who sent the letter, Broussard’s investigation has brought researchers closer than ever to identifying the people who may have brought Minot’s secret photographic mission to an end.

Recent findings suggest that tangerines are not just tasty — they’re a powerhouse of nutrients. Packed with tangy flavor and vibrant orange color, these citrus delights offer a host of health benefits. From boosting your immune system to rejuvenating your skin, tangerines are nutrient-rich allies for your well-being. Let’s delve into their nutritional profile and discover why they’re a smart addition to your diet.

Tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:.

Tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

These tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:.

Sources indicate that tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

Want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

Tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

Industry observers note that are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

These zesty little superheroes are your gut’s fresh best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

Recent findings suggest that tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

Flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

Industry observers note that but wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

Keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related issues and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

Furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

From giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new website called Arkivism aims to make searching for historical imagery considerably easier by bringing more than four million public domain images and videos together in one place.

The free-to-use archive (requires sign-up) includes historical photography from the Library of Congress, NASA imagery, and vintage film reels. Users can search the collection using natural language, describing what they want to find rather than having to know the exact title or filename of an image.

It has been revealed that arkivism also has an interface that will feel familiar to Pinterest users, with an infinite scroll, visual discovery features, and the ability to save images and videos to personal boards. Users can also extract high-resolution stills from archival video clips.

In a recent development, according to its creator, James, the archive right now contains more than four million full-resolution images and over 27,000 searchable film clips. Each asset also includes a backlink to its original source.

“Arkivism started as a fix for my own problem,” James tells PetaPixel, who explains that he used to edit long-form video documentaries on YouTube for the channel History of the Earth.

It has been revealed that “There are millions of incredible public domain assets out there, but they’re scattered across slow, dated archives. Unless you knew the exact filename, finding one specific image could take hours. I wanted one place where I could describe what I needed in plain English and search everything at once.”.

According to recent reports, the project has been developed independently in James’s spare time since July. Despite its size, Arkivism is largely a one-person operation, with AI coding tools helping to make the development process more manageable.

James states the biggest challenge has been building systems capable of collecting material from numerous online sources while ensuring that every asset is properly validated as public domain.

“Above all, every asset has to pass validation checks confirming it’s public domain, because that’s the whole point of the site,” he indicates.

According to recent reports, that emphasis on historical material is also part of the motivation behind the project. With AI-generated imagery becoming increasingly prevalent online, James believes there is particular value in making authentic historical photographs and footage easier to discover.

“I’m not anti-AI, obviously, but there’s real value in looking back, and I think that’s where the site really shines: you can dive endlessly down historical rabbit holes,” he claims.

Although Arkivism borrows some of its interface design from Pinterest, James sees it as both a searchable archive and a visual discovery platform. Unlike traditional institutional archives, users can browse the collection without necessarily knowing what they’re looking for. Unlike Pinterest, however, the experience is not driven by an algorithm and contains no advertising.

Industry observers note that “The site and archive will stay free,” James adds. “But further down the line I strategy to build optional paid tools, such as After Effects and Figma plugins that bring the archive straight into editing software.”.

A post shared by ARKIVISM (@_arkivism).

Industry observers note that the intended audience extends beyond photographers and filmmakers. Researchers, designers, and anyone looking for historical imagery can use the platform to find and download material, with the reassurance that assets have been checked for public domain status.

Arkivism is available now at Arkivism.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that relationships aren’t just about candlelit dinners and cozy sofa nights — they’re complex AF, filled with ups, downs, twists, and turns. From the first flush of love to the settled comfort of commitment, relationships have stages that evolve with time.

Each relationship phase serves a unique purpose, helping you learn more about each other, yourself, and the kind of relationship you want to build. Understanding the dynamics of these stages is crucial for any couple (or throuple!) aiming to develop a lasting bond.

Whether you’re in the throes of a fresh romance or navigating the challenges of a long-term commitment, continue reading to learn how to rock each phase like a pro.

Industry observers note that from those “can’t eat, can’t sleep” early days to the “let’s build an empire” moments, each relationship stage is like a season of your fave drama binge. But, like any good drama, the plot thickens as time passes and things change. Here’s what to expect, month by month:.

Welcome to the love bubble, where everything about your significant other seems nothing short of magical. The positives overshadow any negatives, creating a blissfully skewed balance sheet of love. It lasts from about 6 months to 2 years for most peeps, but many folks say they are still madly in love even after 20 years together!

According to recent reports, research shows that during this stage, the prefrontal cortex, which is crucial for critically judging others, shows decreased activity. In other words, you’re less likely to focus on your partner’s faults and more likely to overlook their flaws.

Industry observers note that lurve also activates specific areas in the brain that are driven by goals and rewards. These areas are rich in dopamine and oxytocin receptors, chemicals that make you feel good and bonded to others. They encourage you to pursue and maintain a relationship because it feels rewarding and fulfilling.

If the euphoric stage is the wild, pulse-racing party of love, the early attachment stage is the cozy after-party where things get real comfortable. In the thrilling initial phase, your brain is doped up on dopamine, but as this initial buzz begins to mellow, a more sophisticated part of the brain starts to step up — the ventral pallidum.

Now, after the first year or so, deeper bonds are formed, helped along by attachment hormones like vasopressin and oxytocin, also fondly known as “the love hormone.” These hormones help transform the electric excitement of fresh love into a warm, enduring attachment.

Recent findings suggest that hold tight because the crisis stage hits around 5 to 7 years, and it’s a true test of your relationship’s resilience. This phase often feels like a rollercoaster, where life’s challenges can either pull you apart or push you closer together. Many couples experience a drift during this time, and how you handle it — either by addressing the issues head-on or continuing to drift — can define your future together.

In a recent development, significant life events, like becoming parents, often occur during this stage and can intensify the pressure. These events can either strengthen your bond through shared responsibilities and mutual love or strain it to the breaking point. Successfully navigating this stage means moving beyond mere survival to fostering a deeper, more meaningful connection.

It has been revealed that if you’ve made it this far, congrats, you’re in the deep attachment stage! Post-crisis, you’re looking at 7 years and beyond where you settle into that deep, comfy love. No more daily fireworks — now it’s about a slow-burning ember that warms the house.

You know each other inside and out, warts and all. It’s about unconditional support, knowing looks across crowded rooms, and being each other’s rock. Welcome to the good life!

Recent findings suggest that every relationship is a blend of sweet and sour and everything in between. Understanding the stages, from the initial euphoria to the deep attachment stage, helps you embrace the journey, keep your bond strong, and prepare your heart for whatever comes next. So buckle up and enjoy the ride — it’ll be worth it!

Weightlifting coach Jarrod Nobbe explains that vibration plates help move blood by stimulating muscle contractions through rapid vibrations.

According to recent reports, as Nobbe adds, movement generally increases blood flow and core temperature, preparing the body for activity. This means vibration plates may be an excellent warm-up activity.

A 2021 study demonstrated that WBV can be an alternative exercise for older adults, boosting the effects of strengthening exercise.

Nobbe notes this is because WBV engages muscles in a way that mimics resistance training.

“The vibrations activate and force muscles to contract and relax multiple times per second, which can lead to gains in muscle strength and endurance over time, especially when combined with specific exercises,” he notes.

Nobbe points to some anecdotal evidence suggesting that regular use of vibration plates may help boost energy levels, possibly thanks to increased blood circulation and enhanced muscle activation.

“Ultimately, I stand by the idea that movement is medicine,” Nobbe says. “Tons of research already proves that regular physical activity boosts mood, mental health, and promotes energy levels.”.

Nobbe states WBV may reduce muscle soreness, stiffness, and inflammation by encouraging blood flow to the muscles. This, he explains, aids in faster recovery post-exercise or injury.

WBV has been shown to improve bone mineral density, which Nobbe points out may positively affect those at risk of osteoporosis.

“The mechanical vibrations stimulate bone cells, potentially leading to increased bone density and strength, delivering the same positive bone health benefits of resistance training,” he notes.

“Unfortunately, vibration plates aren’t a one-stop shop for weight loss,” Nobbe indicates.

He explains that vibration plates alone are unlikely to significantly reduce belly fat without dietary changes and additional exercise.

“While vibration plates can contribute to overall calorie expenditure and muscle activation, targeted fat loss requires a comprehensive approach including diet, cardio exercise, and resistance training,” he notes.

These tips will help you stand on your vibration plate with a slight bend at your knee or perform exercises on top of it.

More research is needed around WBV — AKA what happens when you use a vibration plate — but existing smaller research is promising.

Use your machine carefully, and remember to maintain a healthy lifestyle and workout routine.

This stop-motion horror game proves there's something deeply unsettling about handmade art

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Creativebloq

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that stop-motion animation has been a popular aesthetic in indie games, giving creations a more tactile, handcrafted, and personal touch.
  • It has been revealed that "From studying art, I had just so much more affinity for tangible things and seeing what the materials give me as I'm making things," he tells me.
  • While Talha & Jack Co's previous two games, the Scottish pagan action-adventure Judero and the chill post-apocalyptic robot-mining adventure Mashina, were sprite-based, Abide is more ambitious: a first-person 3D game, so they're scanning the epoxy clay models with photogrammetry, though cutscenes are still being created as stop-motion animation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that stop-motion animation has been a popular aesthetic in indie games, giving creations a more tactile, handcrafted, and personal touch. But while many developers simply emulate this style digitally, two-person indie studio Talha and Jack Co prides itself on making real physical models. For co-founder Jack King-Spooner, creative director of the upcoming game Abide, it's always been what matters most.

It has been revealed that "From studying art, I had just so much more affinity for tangible things and seeing what the materials give me as I'm making things," he tells me. "From my first game 15 years ago, I've always been invested in tangible assets. I couldn't really be bothered drawing pixel art when I could just make a little model and then photograph it from different angles, move it a little bit. It was just so much quicker for me.".

While Talha & Jack Co's previous two games, the Scottish pagan action-adventure Judero and the chill post-apocalyptic robot-mining adventure Mashina, were sprite-based, Abide is more ambitious: a first-person 3D game, so they're scanning the epoxy clay models with photogrammetry, though cutscenes are still being created as stop-motion animation.

"The models are much, much bigger; they've got so much more detail," King-Spooner says, while bringing up a model in his hand as close up to the camera during our video call so that I can see the latex allowing for very realistic textures of skin pores and lips. "I'm always pushing myself with techniques, and finding latest ways to do things. A lot of artists become frozen and immobilised with their craft because they think that there's a right way of doing things, whereas I just like doing things however I can.".

Some of that detail nonetheless does have to be reduced, as a larger, more detailed model could be the equivalent of a super high-res model with 500,000 polygons. "We cut down to like 6,000 polygons so that we can hit good frame rates. They're a bit chunky, but for me they only needed to be recognisable as the same character as in the stop-motion cutscenes. I know lots of people love really tight graphics, but I'd rather spend the time on engaging story and engaging gameplay.".

There are also additional parts that are made for the stop-motion cutscenes. For example, in a scene that requires a close-up of a character washing their hands, they use a larger hand for that shot instead of zooming in on the model's hands, then cut back to the normal model (something Thunderbirds' Jerry Anderson was famous for).

According to recent reports, even with games like Judero, the devs have noted that their stop-motion style has an inherent creepiness, so given that Abide is an "extreme stop motion horror" that includes prosthetic gore effects, King-Spooner is relishing that by doubling down on it. "There's something very abject and horrific about stop motion animation," he states, "It's got this nostalgia, but it's also got this kind of uncanny movement to it which you project life onto.".

To an extent, it also feels like a deliberate response to counter the cosy perceptions people might have of this aesthetic. "A lot of handcrafted games are a bit kind of soft, aren't they? I think with Abide it's really nice that people will think, 'Oh god, a real person, this guy Jack is a real monstrous kind of person that he's made such perverted little dolls doing such horrible things!' I think it adds to the tangibility that it's very much a person's handiwork.".

It nonetheless has an idyllic setting on the surface, set in the St Boniface retreat in the secluded countryside with a group of eight residents from different walks of life in some kind of need of them; at night it descends into full-on horror as you start sneaking around and explore parts of the house you probably shouldn't.

"One aspect which is very disturbing is they're all somehow reflections of myself," King-Spooner admits. "I think it's vital for a creator to recognise that the work you output is somehow autobiographical of yourself. I'm just rather kind of transparent about it.".

In many environments, King-Spooner has also opted to build physical sets or paint textures, such as splattering red paint to make wood textures look bloody or putting on muddy boots and trampling them on white paper to scan.

According to recent reports, if there's a downside to creating physical models and objects, it's that there's often no room to keep them, so after production is over, everything is either chucked out or the clay is mushed up to be reused, although King-Spooner isn't especially precious about preservation. As he bluntly puts it, "We're all going to be dirt in the ground.".

Abide is coming soon to PC, and you can wishlist it on Steam.

Alan Wen is a freelance journalist writing about video games in the form of features, interview, previews, reviews and op-eds. Work has appeared in print including Edge, Official Playstation Magazine, GamesMaster, Games TM, Wireframe, Stuff, and online including Kotaku UK, TechRadar, FANDOM, Rock Paper Shotgun, Digital Spy, The Guardian, and The Telegraph.

Toot Toot! 6 Tips to Prevent Protein Farts

📅 30 Jun 2024 | ⏱️ 4 min read (704 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Greatist

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Protein farts are a common, albeit smelly, side effect of high-protein diets.
  • Protein farts are episodes of flatulence that don’t smell too pleasant!
  • And while these butt whistles may be embarrassing, you’ll be glad to know they’re generally harmless.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Protein farts are a common, albeit smelly, side effect of high-protein diets. They happen because of how proteins are digested. But(t) don’t worry! We have some tips to help you say goodbye to those pungent protein toots without giving up your gains.

Protein farts are episodes of flatulence that don’t smell too pleasant! They’re generally due to upping your protein intake from supplements like protein shakes.

And while these butt whistles may be embarrassing, you’ll be glad to know they’re generally harmless.

Farts consist of different gases. The most stinky odors usually come from your gut bacteria, producing sulfur-containing compounds as they break down food. The main culprit is hydrogen sulfide, which gives off a characteristic rotten egg smell, yum!

But why do your protein choices lead to thunder from down under?

Well, there’s not much evidence that a high-protein diet causes protein farts. However, there’s some anecdotal evidence that supplementary protein — like protein bars, protein shakes, and powder powders — increases flatulence, but it’s likely due to non-protein ingredients like lactose.

In a recent development, supplements containing whey protein or casein are derived from milk and are high in lactose, which can increase flatulence. If your body can’t properly digest lactose, it ends up in your colon, where bacteria feast on it, producing — you guessed it — more gas and cheek flapping.

In a recent development, so, whey protein can throw a curveball for those who are lactose intolerant or sensitive. Surprisingly, it might also stir up digestive drama even for folks who typically handle dairy like champs, potentially due to additives like fart-inducing sweeteners or thickeners.

Some people may also have more significant problems digesting protein. Proteins are significant, complex molecules — breaking them down is no small task for your gut. Plant-based protein supplements, like those based on soya beans, may also worsen flatulence.

FYI: Another reason why flatulence is common with protein powders and supplements is due to the addition of artificial sweeteners in the powders and bars, like sugar alcohols, sucralose, sorbitol, xylitol, and stevia.

If you’re looking to continue your protein regimen without becoming a walking, talking whoopee cushion, here are some strategic adjustments you can make:.

Don’t just dive into the deep end with your protein intake — wade in slowly. Gradually increasing the amount of protein you consume allows your digestive system to adjust without getting overwhelmed. This step-by-step approach can help minimize the likelihood of excessive gas.

Keep the water flowing. Drinking plenty of water is crucial as it helps your digestive system handle higher protein levels more efficiently. Proper hydration aids in the breakdown and absorption of nutrients, which can help prevent gas buildup.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes, your body needs a little extra help. Enzyme supplements like Beano or Lactaid can be game-changers, especially if you consume proteins that your body struggles with. These supplements help break down proteins and lactose, making digestion smoother and less gassy.

Variety isn’t just the spice of life — it can also be the solution to your protein fart problems. If whey protein tends to upset your stomach, explore other options like plant-based or animal-based proteins that might be easier to digest. Diversifying your protein sources can also ensure you get a broad range of nutrients.

What you blend your protein powder with can make a substantial difference. If you’re whipping up a protein shake, be mindful of adding high-fiber fruits and vegetables, as these can also increase gas production. Try to find a balance that allows you to enjoy the benefits of protein and fiber without the extra flatulence.

In a recent development, introducing probiotics into your diet can improve your gut health, which can help manage and reduce gas production. Whether through supplements or probiotic-rich foods like yogurt, kefir, or sauerkraut, boosting your gut flora can aid in better overall digestion and less discomfort from gas.

It has been revealed that protein farts are a rather windy side effect of a high-protein diet, but they don’t have to knock you off course. Try easing into your protein consumption, staying hydrated, diversifying your protein sources, and integrating enzyme supplements or probiotics to max those gains, minus the stink bombs!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Design agency Base Design has created a more compact version of credit card firm Visa’s logo and worked with Displaay Type Foundry on a fresh typeface, as part of a refresh of the brand’s visual identity.
  • While the 2021 Visa wordmark remains unchanged, the refresh included creating a shortened symbol for the brand, rolling out the fresh Visa Sans typeface, and creating a blocky hero graphic to market towards a younger generation.
  • “When you’re working with a brand as iconic as Visa, the challenge isn’t recognition – it’s relevance,” noted Base Design executive creative director Min Lew.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Design agency Base Design has created a more compact version of credit card firm Visa’s logo and worked with Displaay Type Foundry on a fresh typeface, as part of a refresh of the brand’s visual identity.

While the 2021 Visa wordmark remains unchanged, the refresh included creating a shortened symbol for the brand, rolling out the fresh Visa Sans typeface, and creating a blocky hero graphic to market towards a younger generation.

“When you’re working with a brand as iconic as Visa, the challenge isn’t recognition – it’s relevance,” noted Base Design executive creative director Min Lew.

“Our ambition was to build on Visa’s extraordinary equity while giving it a renewed sense of energy and expression, one that feels as relevant to the next generation as it does to the generations who have grown up with it.”.

As part of this strategy, the studio cut the V out of the existing wordmark to function as its own symbol. It will be used on credit cards and appear across digital platforms.

The studio also wrapped it in colourful bar, which will also be used on graphic elements such as posters, and to frame text.

“More than a framing device, the hero graphic device brings movement, direction, and possibility to the identity,” stated Lew.

“This simple gesture becomes the foundation for a visual language that can be energetic at a global sporting event, confident and bold in a B2B environment, or vibrant and elevated for affluent audiences.”.

For Visa Sans, Base Design and Displaay Type Foundry also based the design on the existing logo.

The typeface features rounded edges akin to the rounded corner of the Visa V, and overall, extends “the logo’s character across the wider identity”.

Ultimately, the new identity was created to be used across different smaller, touchpoints according to the team, such as at tap-to-pay stations, at checkout, or online, as the brand appears “for only a moment” in day to day life.

According to recent reports, “We have deep trust and recognition as a brand,” stated Visa chief marketing officer Frank Cooper III. “This refresh gives us an opportunity to build on that.”.

A more subtle approach to logo and branding updates has been popular in recent years, such as at Walmart and Google.

In contrast, the US restaurant chain Cracker Barrel recently took a hard swing at a logo enhancement, which was immediately met with online backlash and promptly scrapped in favour of the original design.

Comment | The future of the ancient city of Palmyra should be determined by its local community

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theartnewspaper

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The ancient city of Palmyra in Syria rose to the world’s attention in May 2015, when Isis militants occupied the site.
  • Industry observers note that in the wake of these atrocities, institutions and governments around the globe launched a dizzying array of projects.
  • It has been revealed that now under a upcoming government, the Syrian antiquities department’s efforts to restore Palmyra – a Unesco World Heritage Site since 1980—are again progressing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The ancient city of Palmyra in Syria rose to the world’s attention in May 2015, when Isis militants occupied the site. Within five months, they had destroyed the Temple of Baalshamin, the Temple of Bel, and the Arch of Triumph—all 2,000-year-old masterpieces. That same year, their murder of Khaled al-Asaad, Palmyra’s retired head of antiquities, sparked worldwide outrage.

Industry observers note that in the wake of these atrocities, institutions and governments around the globe launched a dizzying array of projects. Many focused on preserving the site digitally: the University of California San Diego Library reconstructed the Temple of Bel, for example, and the Université de Lausanne did likewise for the Temple of Baalshamin. Others aimed to one day physically reconstruct what had been lost, including a Russian project to restore the Arch of Triumph. But by the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, none of these plans had been realised.

It has been revealed that now under a upcoming government, the Syrian antiquities department’s efforts to restore Palmyra – a Unesco World Heritage Site since 1980—are again progressing. It has been working to remove illegal constructions and stop illegal excavations, while Palmyra’s local community has been engaged in cleaning the museum’s gardens, among other projects. Meanwhile, a Heritage for Peace project is evaluating the structural condition of buildings in Palmyra’s modern city, which had a pre-war population of 70,000. This renewed momentum once again raises an key question: to what extent should Palmyra’s ancient ruins be physically reconstructed, if at all?

Archaeologist Nour A. Munawar of the University of Amsterdam addressed this problem in 2017, while the war still raged. He emphasised that whether or not to reconstruct should be a decision for Palmyra’s local community, irrespective of where they now live or their political views. Writing in Ex Noxo Journal of Archaeology, he warns that previous reconstruction projects largely left communities out of discussions—such as the limited local consultation when the Stari Most bridge was rebuilt in Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina, or how commercial buildings dominated the reconstruction of post-war Beirut. There is also the danger of “Disneyfication”, a label for artificial, over-polished reconstructions.

It has been revealed that whether to reconstruct has long been a dilemma for war-ravaged places. I recently visited Ypres, Belgium, a city that was totally destroyed during the First World War. In the aftermath, some wondered whether it should be rebuilt as it once appeared, or if its old architecture should be replaced with something more modern. Winston Churchill was in favour of leaving it untouched, as a memorial to the horrors of war. In the end, the local people made the decision: they wanted their Medieval town rebuilt—even if, for the most part, only the facades reflected the pre-war era.

Industry observers note that A 2024 study by Benjamin Isakhan, a professor of international politics at Deakin University, Melbourne, and Lynn Meskell, a professor of anthropology at the University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, provides an insight into how Syrians feel about this issue. After surveying 1,600 Aleppo residents, they found that almost all were proud of their cultural heritage, but Aleppines prioritised “safety and security”, “electricity, water and other services” and “unemployment and poverty” over “heritage protection and reconstruction” in terms of urgency.

And although 98% agreed that damaged or destroyed heritage sites should be restored or reconstructed, opinions varied on how: 17% wanted them to appear as “first built”, 24% as they appeared before the war, and 30% wanted them “restored and reconstructed into a newly introduced and more modern structure”. Heritage experts’ preference for authenticity could therefore go against some local wishes. Overwhelmingly, Aleppines also wanted Syrian control over rebuilding their heritage, not global agencies, NGOs, and foreign governments, Isakhan and Meskell note in the International Journal of Heritage Studies.

Industry observers note that palmyra is now a symbol of Syria, known worldwide. But whether the city’s rebuilt heritage retains its battle scars, becomes “Disneyfied”, or something in between, should be a local choice, as should whether any reconstruction is prioritised over more pressing needs. As time passes, an increasing number of voices will come into play—the latest Syrian government, foreign governments, international bodies, NGOs and cultural heritage experts—all providing much-needed money, aid and advice. We must hope that the local community is not lost in the mix. In the end, it must be the people of Palmyra who decide their city’s fate.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, is it time to give your hairstyle and scalp a breath of fresh air? Say hello to the undercut hairstyle, a fashion-forward solution that can elevate your look and promote skin health.

By significantly reducing hair volume, undercuts allow for improved air circulation around the scalp. The result? Less trapped heat and moisture — factors that can contribute to fungal infections, scalp acne, dandruff, and dermatitis.

Whether you’re battling irritation or want to give your “do” a new lease on life, continue reading to learn how undercut hairstyles can be your ally in style and scalp health.

An undercut involves shaving or cutting hair very short on the sides or back of the head while leaving the hair on top longer.

Originally popular in men’s hairstyling, the undercut has crossed gender boundaries and gained popularity among peeps seeking a hairstyle that stands out.

Industry observers note that it’s a style that offers a stark contrast and is often used to add an edge to an otherwise conventional look. So whether it’s a side undercut, undercut pixie, mullet undercut, or nape undercut, these hairstyles for women, men, and folks of all genders enhance individuality while offering practical benefits like reduced drying time and less hair maintenance.

Choosing an undercut means embracing a hairstyle with a “heady” mix of aesthetic and practical benefits. Here’s why an undercut might be the refreshing change you need.

Ready to turn heads? The standout feature of an undercut is undoubtedly its unique appearance. Hidden under the longer layers, it packs a punch of boldness you can flaunt or conceal — whatever fits your vibe. You can control the reveal, whether you’re showcasing that edgy undercut for a night out or keeping it classy for the office.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hickeys, or as scientists call them, subdermal hematomas, are love’s graffiti.
  • A hickey, medically known as a subdermal contusion or hematoma, is simply a bruise that forms as a result of vigorous kissing or sucking on soft skin, typically around the neck.
  • Sources indicate that from a medical standpoint, hickeys are intriguing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hickeys, or as scientists call them, subdermal hematomas, are love’s graffiti. If you’ve ever scrambled for scarves or turtlenecks, welcome to the kissing booth of knowledge! Join us as we navigate the lifecycle of hickeys, from their eye-catching start to their subtle fade, and learn how to speed up their departure.

A hickey, medically known as a subdermal contusion or hematoma, is simply a bruise that forms as a result of vigorous kissing or sucking on soft skin, typically around the neck. This intense suction causes the tiny blood vessels under the skin, a.k.a. capillaries, to burst and release blood into the surrounding tissues. The immediate result? An unmistakable red or purple mark that gradually shifts to a darker shade as it heals.

Sources indicate that from a medical standpoint, hickeys are intriguing. They showcase the skin’s sensitivity and the body’s rapid response to minor vascular injury. Not so romantic when you think about it scientifically, right? But hey, it’s all part of the human experience of showing affection — or something like that.

In a recent development, when you get a hickey, your body starts a healing process that resembles how it deals with other bruises. Here’s a more detailed look at each stage of a hickey’s life cycle.

Immediately after the passionate moment, a hickey appears on the skin, screaming in shades of bright red or deep purple. This initial coloration is due to blood from the ruptured capillaries pooling beneath the skin’s surface in response to the suction. It’s your skin’s way of signaling that there’s been some minor internal damage in that area.

As the hickey begins to heal, it undergoes a whole wardrobe of color transformations, showcasing your body’s metabolic process at work.

Initially, the hickey darkens as the blood begins to oxidize. Then, after a few days, the body starts to break down and reabsorb the blood, so it turns lighter — going from blue to green to brown and, finally, mellow yellow. This rainbow journey reflects the breakdown of hemoglobin, the iron-containing substance in the blood, into biliverdin and bilirubin.

According to recent reports, finally, your hickey starts to ghost you. Over a week or two, depending on factors like your skin type, overall health, how severe the hickey was., and how your body rides the healing waves, the last traces of your hickey fade into nothing.

It has been revealed that during this stage, the body’s immune system clears away the remaining by-products of the broken-down blood. White blood cells swoop in like a cleanup crew at a festival, gobbling up and digesting the debris in a process called phagocytosis, while increased blood flow to the area helps to flush out the remnants.

In a recent development, need a hickey gone yesterday? Here’s how to help your hickey heal. Start with a cold pack — grab a spoon from the freezer or a chilled gel pack and gently press it against your hickey. This will help reduce any swelling and scatter the blood pooling under your skin, which can help minimize that bold bruise.

After using cold treatment for the first 48 hours, it’s time to turn up the heat. Switch to warm compresses to get the blood flowing smoothly again. A few minutes a few times a day invites more circulation to the hickey zone, helping you hustle through healing and clear out the blood remnants more swiftly.

Sources indicate that you can also try a dab of comfrey ointment. Research reveals it may reduce bruise size and coloration for some peeps.

It has been revealed that caught off guard? A little concealer or foundation over the hickey makes it less noticeable.

According to recent reports, not into makeup? Scarves and high-necked shirts are also great accessories for your camouflage arsenal.

Typically, a hickey will last anywhere from 5 days to 2 weeks, depending on its severity and your body’s healing capabilities.

According to recent reports, communication is key! Let your partner know your feelings about receiving a hickey — some might find it fun, while others may prefer to keep their necks clear.

It has been revealed that while generally harmless, hickeys can sometimes lead to complications like skin infections or, very rarely, blood clots. It’s best to keep the affection gentle to avoid any problems.

Hickeys are nothing more than bruises in disguise. They start as bright red to purple love stamps and gradually fade over several days to a couple of weeks. Speed up the process with heat and cold packs or a splodge of comfrey cream.

Remember, the best approach to handling hickeys — like all aspects of relationships — is communication and care. So go forth, love responsibly, and keep a scarf handy, just in case!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

National Gallery of Australia, Canberra.

Industry observers note that the American Friends of the National Gallery of Australia bought this sculpture by Simone Leigh last year from Matthew Marks Gallery in Fresh York. The monumental bronze, measuring 3.3m long and 1.5m tall, is named after the Nigerian American artist and actress Okwui Okpokwasili. It highlights a reclining woman in a cast raffia skirt, exploring the resilience and cultural memory that merges the semi-abstract female form with the African vernacular. This cast is the second from an edition of two (with one artist’s proof). In 2022, Leigh became the first Black woman to represent the US at the Venice Biennale.

Untitled (wharf, Gloucester, Massachusetts) (1934) by Mark Rothko.

Cape Ann Museum/Christopher Rothko.

Cape Ann Museum, Gloucester, Massachusetts.

Christopher Rothko, the son of the artist Mark Rothko (1903-70), says that while his father thought “all art was inherently of its time”, sometimes “even with a master of abstraction like Mark Rothko, art can also be inherently of its place”. He is referring to this painting—an atmospheric early watercolour-and-gouache work depicting the harbour in Gloucester—which Christopher recently donated to the Cape Ann Museum from his private collection. Mark Rothko frequently summered on Cape Ann, painting alongside two other Fresh York artists: his mentor, Milton Avery, and his friend Adolph Gottlieb. This painting is included in Avery, Gottlieb & Rothko: By the Sea—a touring exhibition at the moment on view at the Phillips Collection in Washington, DC (until 24 January 2027).

Arc-en-ciel no. 5 (1913-14) by Robert Delaunay.

Sources indicate that it may not be instantly recognisable, but the lilac spire behind the rainbow in this painting is the Eiffel Tower—the tallest building in the world when the work was painted by Robert Delaunay (1885-1941). The French artist was the husband of Sonia Delaunay, and in 1912 they co-founded the short-lived Orphism movement—an offshoot of Cubism that prized bright colours and geometric shapes. This vivid oil-on-canvas work, measuring 35cm by 40cm, is one of several variations of the composition and demonstrates Delaunay moving away from strict geometry to a looser, more expressive and rhythmic style. The painting, which sold at Christie’s in 2025 for $317,500 (with fees) from the collection of Arnold and Joan Saltzman, was exhibited by the London-based dealer Willoughby Gerrish at Tefaf Maastricht in March—where the sale to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, was initially agreed.
